instruction: You are a strategic corporate innovation advisor. Analyse the company profile and survey responses, then respond ONLY with a valid JSON object containing maturity_score, opportunities, next_steps, and key_weaknesses.

answers.companyDescription: Boutique litigation firm handling complex commercial disputes, arbitration, and white-collar defense. Team of 18 litigators. Managing 60+ active cases with thousands of documents per case. Seeking e-discovery platform with predictive coding for document review prioritization. The organization has significant capital, talent depth, and existing technology infrastructure, but internal processes are designed for stability and risk management—not speed.
answers.pastInitiatives: We have never run a formal innovation initiative. Problems are solved ad-hoc as they arise, usually by the most directly affected team member. There is no dedicated budget, no structured ideation process, and no track record of experimenting with new technologies or business models beyond basic operational necessity.
answers.strategicGoals: Our industry is facing structural decline due to technological disruption and changing consumer behavior. We cannot rely on incremental improvements to our legacy business—we need to identify entirely new value propositions that leverage our brand, customer relationships, or operational capabilities in adjacent spaces where demand is growing, not shrinking.
answers.additionalContext: Meridian operates primarily in domestic commercial law and faces increasing competition from mid-tier firms adopting faster, AI-driven workflows. The firm's long time horizon allows for exploration of entirely new service lines like regulatory compliance consulting.
answers.teamSize: We have a corporate innovation division with 50+ staff spanning research scientists, engineers, designers, and strategy professionals. The division manages a portfolio of 15 active innovation projects at various maturity stages, from early-stage research collaborations with universities to near-commercialization products. Annual innovation budget is managed through a formal portfolio governance process with stage-gate funding decisions.

opportunities.title: Process Automation via Low-Risk Adjacent Tech (eDiscovery)
opportunities.rationale: Given the low digital maturity and high regulatory environment, adopting incremental e-discovery tools or basic AI for contract review is a conservative first step. This leverages existing technology infrastructure without requiring massive upfront investment or disrupting core legal practice.

first_actions: Conduct feasibility study on using off-the-shelf e-discovery software integration (cost under $50k).
Pilot predictive coding for document prioritization on a single, low-risk case category.
Conduct regulatory compliance review with legal team to ensure alignment with applicable regulations
execution_plan.success_metric: Reduce average time spent on initial document review by 15% in the pilot scope.
milestones: Q3: Feasibility report completed and preliminary vendor selection.

opportunities.title: Service Diversification into Regulatory Compliance Consulting
opportunities.rationale: Leveraging the firm's legal expertise in complex white-collar defense to offer a new, adjacent service line focused on regulatory compliance advisory. This is an incremental step that minimizes market entry risk by utilizing existing talent and infrastructure.

first_actions: Identify 2 high-growth compliance niches (e.g., ESG reporting)
Develop a standardized service offering template and pitch deck.
resources_needed: Cross-training existing litigators in regulatory framework analysis.
execution_plan.success_metric: Secure 2 retainer clients for the new compliance consulting line within Year 1.
milestones: Q1 (Year 2): Achieve $50k in recurring revenue from adjacent services.

opportunities.title: Entry into Global Arbitration Tech Platform (Market Diversification)
opportunities.rationale: A bold move involving the development of a proprietary SaaS platform specifically designed for streamlined, cross-jurisdictional arbitration management. While high risk and requiring significant investment, this addresses the strategic need for diversification by creating a scalable product that moves the company beyond pure hourly billing.

first_actions: Establish a dedicated, small 'tiger team' of engineers/strategists.
Develop a Minimum Viable Product (MVP) focusing on one specific international arbitration mechanism.
Conduct regulatory compliance review with legal team to ensure alignment with applicable regulations
resources_needed: Seed funding allocation ($50k reserved from budget)
execution_plan.success_metric: Achieve 10 paying pilot clients using the proprietary platform within 18 months.
milestones: Q3: MVP development completed and internal testing finished.
Q1 (Year 2): Launch paid beta with initial revenue targets met.

next_steps.action: Launch a structured, low-stakes ideation workshop focused solely on service diversification opportunities.
Finalize and secure budget for the incremental e-discovery pilot project based on Q3 findings.
Initiate a talent assessment to identify skill gaps required for future technology integration (e.g., data science or product management).

key_weaknesses: Lack of formal innovation process leading to reactive problem-solving.
Insufficient budget allocated for proactive technological experimentation and long-term R&D.
Low digital maturity hindering the ability to adopt advanced technologies like predictive coding at scale.
